newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's CITIC Pacific buys into China Light.
newsitem.headline: HK's CITIC Pacific buys into China Light.

text.p: Hong Kong's CITIC Pacific Ltd said on Tuesday it would acquire a substantial stake in one of Hong Kong's two electricity generators for an outlay of about HK$16.25 billion (US$2.08 billion).

In an announcement widely anticipated in the Hong Kong stock market, CITIC Pacific said it would acquire 497,664,000 new shares in China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) at HK$32.66 each, representing a 20 percent stake in CLP's enlarged share capital.
The issue price represents a discount of about 3.1 percent to CLP's closing price of HK$33.70 per share on Monday.
Trading in both companies was suspended on Tuesday.
Analysts said the move was a logical one for both companies. It was in line with CITIC's recent diversification strategy and may give CLP a helping hand in the China market.
CLP chairman Michael Kadoorie echoed these views.

"CLP's financial strength and capable professional management together with CITIC Pacific's relationships in the PRC (People's Republic of China) will put CLP in a very strong position to take full advantage of the substantial opportunities in the power industry in the PRC."
"CITIC Pacific has confirmed it will cooperate with CLP to procure power projects in the PRC."
He said CLP would use the proceeds for new investments in China and elsewhere in Asia.
Thomas Chesser, director of regional power research at BZW Asia said CLP's latest project was an obvious beneficiary.

"I think the obvious synergy is that China Light's Shandong project (in northeast China) which is huge -- it is 3,200 megawatts -- (it) has been stuck for almost three years and the synergy would be that if CITIC took a position it could use its mainland influence to push that project ahead."

CITIC Pacific, the Hong Kong-listed arm of China's powerful state trading giant China International Trust and Investment Corp, is a diversified group with interests ranging from trading and distribution to property investment and aviation.

CITIC Pacific said the placement would be divided into two tranches. The first comprises 199,065,600 new shares representing 10 percent of CLP's existing share capital and is pursuant to the mandate granted to CLP directors.
The second tranche comprises 298,598,400 new shares and represents 15 percent of the existing share capital of CLP and is dependent on CLP shareholders' approval.
The holding was a long-term investment, CITIC Pacific, which undertook not to dispose of any of the new CLP shares for at least three years, it said.
Earlier this month, Hong Kong conglomerate Hutchison Whampoa Ltd raised its stake in Hong Kong's other power utility, Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd triggering a mandatory general offer.
CITIC said in a statement the tranches would be funded out of internal resources and bank borrowings.
Analysts had earlier said CITIC, which raised its stake in Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd to 25 percent from 10 percent in the middle of last year, may be fairly strapped for cash.
This led many to speculate CITIC would look for some type of stock swap possibly or even the creation of a holding company in which more shares are issued to finance its ambitions for CLP.
CITIC has applied for a resumption in trading of its shares from Wednesday. ($1=HK$7.8)
